text:
Maya Chen: Heads-up — I rolled nvidia-driver 537.41 + CUDA 12.1 to us-west-2 GPU pool (canary then staged). Within ~20m we started seeing NCCL timeouts and intermittent OOMKilled on several A100 nodes. Reverting canary now.
Aj Patel: On it. Do we have a correlation ID or a node list?
Maya Chen: Incident log: deploy-bot created incident T-4312. Affected nodes: gw-a100-*-usw2 (5 nodes), pods mostly high-seq workloads. I saw kernel dmesg showing mm_fault and some pci errors.
deploy-bot: [incident T-4312] created by Maya Chen — priority P2 — quiet window enabled.
Keisha Gomez: Noted. This smells like a driver <-> kernel <-> NCCL regression combo. We should pin the fleet to the previous known-good driver and gate further rollouts.
Lorenzo: Agreed. Suggest two immediate actions: 1) pin apt/yum packages on prod nodes, 2) add kube node label + admission webhook to block node images with driver 537.x until we validate.
Keisha Gomez: For immediate pinning (Debian/Ubuntu):
```
# hold package versions
sudo apt-mark hold nvidia-driver-537 cuda-toolkit-12-1
# add apt preferences (example)
cat >/etc/apt/preferences.d/nvidia-pin <<EOF
Package: nvidia-*
Pin: version 535.*
Pin-Priority: 1001
EOF
```
And for RHEL/CentOS with yum/dnf:
```
# install yum-plugin-versionlock then
sudo yum versionlock add nvidia-driver-537* cuda-12.1*
```
These commands will prevent auto-upgrades during the rollback window.
Aj Patel: We also need to update our automation (salt/ansible) so future runs don't undo the holds. I'll push playbooks to set hold flags in the state.
oncall-sre: I'm patching the node selector on staging and stopping further staged rollouts. Also adding node label: `gpu.redwood.com/driver=535` and a gate that prevents nodes labeled with driver!=535 from joining the prod pool.
Maya Chen: Can we get a quick compatibility matrix logged somewhere so PMs/infra know which combos are validated? Right now it's murky which kernel versions tolerate the new driver.
Keisha Gomez: I'll draft a lockstep matrix snippet. Minimal for now (plain list):
- driver 535.x + CUDA 12.0 — validated on kernels 5.15, 5.10
- driver 537.x + CUDA 12.1 — reported regressions on kernels 5.15, 5.13 (needs 5.19+ or vendor patch)
- fallback: use driver 535 + cuda 12.0 for production until QA signs off on driver 537 on each kernel family
Lorenzo: We should codify that into our release gating: change-levels: driver, cuda, kernel. Roll only if the matrix has explicit PASS for that triplet. If not PASS -> need canary + longer soak or block.
Aj Patel: I'm going to add a temporary admission hook to the cluster manager — reject nodes where `node.metadata.labels['gpu.redwood.com/driver']` != `535` for prod clusters. Will also add a rollout policy in the console to require sign-off.
Maya Chen: For rollback, I'm reverting the driver packages on the 5 impacted nodes and restarting kubelet. Will monitor NCCL errors.
Lorenzo: Also please capture GPU kernel ring buffer and upload to the incident ticket. Use `sudo dmesg -T | tail -n 200` and `nvidia-smi -q` outputs.
Maya Chen: Uploaded logs to T-4312. Early signal: NCCL timeouts dropped to zero after revert on 3/5 nodes; two nodes still flapping — doing a full node reboot there.
oncall-sre: Reboots completed, flapping stopped on those two. Marking incident as mitigated for now, will keep P2.
Keisha Gomez: Next steps (action items):
- Keisha: produce full matrix doc + start a short validation run for 537.x on kernel 5.19/5.20 in staging (ETA 48h)
- Aj: update Ansible states to set package holds and ensure idempotent behavior (ETA 3h)
- Lorenzo: push admission hook gating to prod clusters and update rollout policy (ETA 1h)
- Maya: finish postmortem notes in T-4312 and add repro steps for QA (ETA 24h)
Maya Chen: Thanks all. Please ack if you have any blocking issues. :thumbsup:
Aj Patel: Ack.
Keisha Gomez: Ack.
Lorenzo: Ack.
oncall-sre: Ack.
Maya Chen: One more note — link to pinning playbook we're updating: https://redwood.internal/infra/pinning-playbook (putting TODOs there).
Lorenzo: We should consider a longer-term strategy: automated compat testing matrix that runs driver/cuda/kernel permutations on a small canary fleet nightly. I'll open a project ticket.
Maya Chen: Sounds good. Closing thread for now — will reopen if regressions return.
